meta.title: Hexaequo
meta.tagline: An abstract strategy game for two

home.purpose: Hexaequo is a free abstract strategy board game for two players. There is no fixed board: you build it as you play, one tile at a time. Play on one device, against the computer, or online with a friend.
home.credit: A game created by Piero Barrette

rules.title: Rules
rules.lede: Hexaequo is played on a board that does not exist yet: the players build it as they go, one tile at a time.
rules.goalIntro: You win the moment any one of these is true at the end of your turn:
rules.goalCleared: your opponent has no piece left on the board — even if pieces remain in their reserve.
rules.materialText: Each player owns 9 tiles, 6 disks and 3 rings in their colour. Black moves first.
rules.setupText: The two black tiles and the two white tiles are laid against each other in a compact block of four. A disk sits on each of the two opposite tiles of that block — the only pair that do not touch — each on a tile of its own colour. Those pieces come out of the reserves, so each player starts the game holding 7 tiles and 5 disks.
rules.setupCaption: The opening position. Black's disk is top right, White's is bottom left; the two tiles carrying them are the only ones in the block that are not neighbours.
rules.turnText: On your turn you must carry out exactly one of three actions: lay a tile, place a piece, or move a piece. Passing is not allowed, and whatever you do must change the position.
rules.tileText: Take a tile from your reserve and lay it on any empty cell that touches at least two tiles already on the board. The colours of those neighbours do not matter — only how many there are.
rules.tileCaption: The dashed cells each touch two existing tiles, so any of them may take a tile. The cell marked in red touches only one, so it may not.
rules.placeText: Take a disk or a ring from your reserve and place it on an empty tile of your own colour. Placing a ring costs you something extra: you must hand back one enemy disk you have already captured. It returns to your opponent's reserve and no longer counts towards your total of six.
rules.placeCaption: Black may place on either empty black tile, never on a white one. The ring is only available once Black holds at least one captured white disk to give back.
rules.diskText: A disk does one of two things. It either takes one step onto an adjacent empty tile, or it makes a chain of one or more jumps. A jump crosses one adjacent occupied tile — friendly or enemy — and lands on the next tile in the same straight line, which must exist and be empty. Every enemy piece crossed is captured and taken off at once; friendly pieces crossed are simply flown over. You may stop after any jump in the chain.
rules.diskCaption: Black jumps the white disk and lands on the empty tile beyond it, capturing as it passes. A second jump is available from there, and Black may take it or stop.
rules.diskLoop: One restriction keeps chains finite: within a single chain a disk may not land again on a cell it has already occupied since its last capture. Hopping back and forth over friendly pieces is therefore impossible, while a genuine capturing chain that loops back to its starting cell remains legal.
rules.ringText: A ring makes one leap, of exactly two tiles' distance — twelve possible destinations on a full board. Nothing can block it: the cell it passes over may hold any piece, or may not even hold a tile. If an enemy piece stands on the arrival tile, it is captured. A ring may never finish on a piece of its own colour.
rules.ringCaption: All twelve cells at distance two from the ring. It may leap onto any of them that carries a tile, capturing an enemy piece there.
rules.finePrintTitle: Points that are easy to get wrong
rules.finePrint1: Tile colour only restricts placement. A piece that moves may finish on any empty tile, whatever its colour.
rules.finePrint2: Captured pieces leave the game, with one exception: a disk handed back to pay for a ring. Captured rings never come back.
rules.finePrint3: A jump is not compulsory. You may play a quiet move even when a capture is on offer.
rules.finePrint4: The board tops out at 18 tiles, nine from each player.
rules.drawText: The game is a draw — ExAequo — if the player to move has no legal move at all, or if the same position occurs three times.
rules.figureLegend: Black tile, white tile, disk, ring.

legal.contactBody: For any question, or to request access to or deletion of your data, write to {email}.
legal.privacyIntro: Hexaequo is an online board game. This page explains what we collect, why, and what you can do about it. We show no advertising and sell no data.
legal.p1Body: Without an account, nothing about you reaches our servers: your preferences (language, theme, sound, move aid) stay in your browser’s local storage. If you sign in with Google we receive your Google account identifier, your email address and your display name, and we keep the nickname you choose on Hexaequo. We also record your games: the moves played, the result, the time control and your rating.
legal.p2Body: Your Google identifier only lets us recognise you from one visit to the next. The email address lets us reach you about your account. Games and ratings are what make the game and the leaderboard work. We do no profiling and no targeted advertising.
legal.p3Body: Our servers and database are hosted by Render, in the United States. Your data is therefore processed outside Canada and may be subject to the laws of the hosting country.
legal.p4Body: Nothing is sold or rented. Your nickname, your rating and your finished games are visible to other players — that is what a leaderboard is. Your email address never is.
legal.p5Body: For as long as your account exists. You may ask for it to be deleted at any time: the account and its email address are erased, and games already played are detached from your identity.
legal.p6Body: You may ask to see your data, to correct it, to have it deleted, or to receive a portable copy. We answer within thirty days.
legal.p7Body: We use no advertising cookies and no third-party analytics. Your browser’s local storage holds only your preferences and your session.
legal.termsIntro: By using Hexaequo you agree to the following. The service is offered free of charge, as is.
legal.t1Body: The game is open to everyone. If you are under 14, ask a parent before creating an account.
legal.t2Body: You choose your nickname freely, provided it is not abusive, hateful, misleading about who you are, or intended to impersonate another player. We may rename or close an account that breaks this rule.
legal.t3Body: You may not use a program to play rated games for you, repeatedly abandon games to avoid a loss, or arrange results with an opponent to distort the ratings. Doing so may cost you your rating or your account.
legal.t4Body: The service may be interrupted, changed or discontinued without notice. We guarantee neither continuous availability nor permanent retention of games.
legal.t5Body: Hexaequo is provided without warranty of any kind. We cannot be held responsible for the loss of data, of a rating, or of an account.
legal.t6Body: These terms may change. The date at the top of the page shows the last revision; continuing to play means accepting it.
